classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish sufficient congruence information from distractors and put corresponding vertices in matching order.

content.prompt: In each of the following, state which triangle is congruent to $\triangle ABC$, giving the appropriate congruence test as a reason.

spec.description: Four comparison triangles in source order, ABC, DEF, GHJ and KLM. Ordinary source blue outlines are rendered black under house style. No shading.
spec.mathematics: ABC: AC one tick, AB two, BC three. DEF: DE and EF one, DF three. GHJ: GH one, GJ two, HJ three. KLM: KL and LM two, KM three.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels and side marks are permanent givens; no selected answer is shown.

answer.worked: The marked sides give $AB=GJ$, $BC=JH$ and $AC=GH$. Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle GJH$ by SSS.

spec.description: Four comparison triangles in source order, ABC, PQR, STU and XYZ. Angle labels lie inside their specified sectors. Ordinary outlines and annotations are black; no shading.
spec.mathematics: ABC: AB one tick, BC two, angle ABC alpha. PQR: PR one, RQ two, angle PQR alpha. STU: ST one, SU two, angle STU alpha. XYZ: XY two, YZ one, angle XYZ alpha.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied marks and alpha labels only; no answer is shown.

answer.worked: The markings give $AB=ZY$, $BC=YX$ and $\angle ABC=\angle ZYX=\alpha$. These are two sides and their included angle, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle ZYX$ by SAS.

spec.description: Four comparison triangles in source order, ABC, DLP, MNO and STR. Alpha and beta remain in their respective angle sectors. Ordinary marks are black; no shading.
spec.mathematics: ABC: BC one tick, B alpha, C beta. DLP: DP one tick, D alpha, P beta. MNO: NO one tick, M alpha, N beta. STR: ST one tick, S alpha, R beta.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied side and angle information only.

answer.worked: The markings give $\angle ABC=\angle LDP=\alpha$, $\angle ACB=\angle LPD=\beta$ and $BC=DP$. The equal side is a matching side for these equal angles, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle LDP$ by AAS.

spec.sourceRegion: Exercise 7C question 4(d), continuation at top of page
spec.description: Four comparison triangles ABC, PQR, TUV and WOS in one horizontal row. Right-angle squares are derived from the incident edges. Ordinary outlines and marks are black; no shading.
spec.mathematics: ABC: right angle A, AB one tick, AC two. PQR: right angle R, PR two ticks, RQ one. TUV: right angle U, TV one tick, TU two. WOS: right angle O, WO and OS two ticks.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied right angles, side marks and vertex labels remain visible; no solution marks are added.

answer.worked: The markings give $AB=RQ$, $AC=RP$ and $\angle BAC=\angle QRP=90^\circ$. The equal angle is included between the two equal sides, so $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle RQP$ by SAS.
